seo.title: Ecuador & Galápagos Summer Program | Pacific Discovery
seo.description: Ecuador & Galápagos in 4 weeks: a community stay in Agato, the Quilotoa crater loop, Spanish and canyoning in Baños, Jatunyacu rafting and Galápagos snorkeling. Ages 17–22.

hero.headline: From the Andes to the Galápagos in one summer
hero.intro: Live and volunteer in the Andean village of Agato, hike the Quilotoa crater loop, raft the Jatunyacu River and snorkel at Kicker Rock in the Galápagos.

itinerary.heading: Week by week
itinerary.note: This is a guide to what you can expect to do on program. The order in which activities occur might vary. Itineraries are subject to change.

weeks.title: Quito & the Agato community
weeks.body:
You’ll meet your Program Instructors in Quito for orientation, then take the Teleférico, a cable car above the city, for a hike and a day exploring Quito.

Next we take the bus north to Agato, a Kichwa village in the highlands, and settle in. Over the following days we join in service-learning and community immersion, working alongside local families on a community development project and taking part in daily life.

weeks.title: Quilotoa crater & Baños
weeks.body:
After a final day in Agato, we stop at Otavalo Market on the way to Quilotoa and spend the night in cabañas. In the morning we hike the Quilotoa crater loop, then take the bus to Baños.

In Baños we take Spanish lessons each morning. Afternoons bring salsa lessons, a hike to Casa del Árbol, hot springs and a canyoning session. The week ends with a bus ride to Tena.
weeks.imageAlt: Two students with arms outstretched above a crater lake

weeks.title: Jatunyacu rafting to the Galápagos
weeks.location: Tena → Misahuallí → Quito → San Cristóbal, Ecuador
weeks.body:
Our two-day rafting trip on the Jatunyacu River includes a night camping, before we transfer to the Sinchi Warmi center in Misahuallí. Here we have a group session, cultural activities, a morning of volunteering and a co-op visit, with a waterfall hike or more cultural activities.

On the way back to Quito we stop at Papallacta Hot Springs. Then we fly to San Cristóbal in the Galápagos to snorkel at La Lobería, and join a service project at Hacienda Tranquila.
weeks.imageAlt: Group paddling a raft through river rapids

weeks.title: San Cristóbal, Isabela & Santa Cruz
weeks.location: San Cristóbal → Floreana → Isabela → Santa Cruz, Galápagos
weeks.body:
We visit Kicker Rock and a turtle spot from San Cristóbal, then take the boat to Floreana and on to Isabela.

On Isabela we hike a volcano, take a Tintoreras tour and hold our program wrap. Then we take the boat to Santa Cruz for our last night, and transfer to Baltra the next morning, where students depart from Seymour Airport.
weeks.imageAlt: Students in wetsuits on a boat beside tall sea rocks

faq.heading: Questions we get about this program

items.q: How fit do I need to be?
items.a: Be ready to try the Quilotoa crater loop hike, canyoning, two days of rafting, a volcano hike on Isabela and snorkeling, plus some physical work on community and service projects.

items.q: What is the stay in Agato like?
items.a: Agato is a Kichwa village in Ecuador’s northern highlands. You’ll stay in the community, work alongside local families on a community development project and take part in daily life.
Mostly hostels and guesthouses, plus a community stay in Agato, cabañas at Quilotoa, the Sinchi Warmi center in Misahuallí and a night camping on the rafting trip.
Yes. You’ll have Spanish lessons each morning during our time in Baños.

Tuition covers all in-country transport, accommodation, meals, and the activities and entry fees in the itinerary. It doesn't cover international flights, visas, travel insurance, spending money, optional college credit or optional activities.

items.q: How much spending money should I bring?
items.a: About $100 a week for snacks, laundry, personal shopping and optional activities. It varies from student to student.

items.q: Can I stay in touch with home?
items.a: Yes. We encourage keeping phones on flight mode so you stay present, and wifi is available where we stay in cities and towns. There will also be a photo album that students and instructors can upload photos and video to, so parents and caregivers can stay up to date.

items.q: Do I need a passport or visa?
items.a: Your passport must be valid for more than 6 months after the program ends. All the information you need in regard to visas will be available in your student portal.

safety.heading: For parents: how we keep students safe

items.title: 24/7 Emergency Line
items.body: Parents, students and instructors can reach a real person at any hour. Every call is logged and passed to our on-call staff member by phone.

items.title: Wilderness First Aid & Live Risk Assessment
items.body: All our instructors hold Wilderness First Aid (WFA) certification and have extensive training in group leadership and risk management.

items.title: Accredited Safety Systems
items.body: Our safety systems are assessed and accredited by the Gap Year Association (USA), Year Out Group (UK) and OutdoorsMark (NZ). Students on Go Overseas voted us one of the top gap year providers for safety.

items.title: Insurance & Health
items.body: Comprehensive travel insurance is required, covering medical costs and emergency evacuation. Check vaccinations with your doctor, and pack a first-aid kit and any personal medication. Our instructors can't legally give students any medication.
